name: Batswana Seswaa
description: Seswaa, pounded meat, is Botswana's national dish, and its real defining character is genuine simplicity - just meat, water, and salt, simmered for hours until the meat falls apart, then pounded directly in its own reduced cooking liquid, not drained. Real sources are explicit that adding much beyond onion and bay leaf is considered a departure from the dish; the long, patient simmer, not seasoning, is what makes it what it is.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Beef, chuck, short ribs, boneless, separable lean and fat, trimmed to 0" fat, all grades, raw

ingredients.ingredient: Beef, chuck, short ribs, boneless, separable lean and fat, trimmed to 0" fat, all grades, raw

steps_detailed: Combine the beef, onion, bay leaf, and salt in a heavy pot with enough water to just cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a bare simmer, cover, and cook 2.5-3 hours, until the meat is completely fall-apart tender and most of the liquid has reduced.

Remove the onion and bay leaf, then pound or shred the meat directly in the pot, working it into the remaining concentrated liquid until it forms a moist, cohesive, shredded mass - this real technique, not extra seasoning, is what defines seswaa.

name: Batswana Pap
description: Pap, a stiff maize porridge, is the essential companion to seswaa and most Batswana meals, real technique showering the cornmeal in gradually while beating constantly to build a smooth, dense texture.
steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Gradually beat in the remaining cornmeal, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick and it pulls away from the sides of the pot.

name: Batswana Morogo
description: Morogo, cooked wild spinach or leafy greens, is the real, traditional vegetable side served alongside seswaa and pap, real technique keeping the seasoning simple - onion and a little oil - so the greens' own flavor carries the dish.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil 3-4 minutes.
Add the spinach and a splash of water, and simmer 10-12 minutes until tender.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil 3-4 minutes.

name: Batswana Bogobe Jwa Lerotse
description: Bogobe jwa lerotse, a sour melon porridge, is a genuine Batswana specialty, real technique cooking real melon or squash down into the sorghum porridge, which gives it its distinctive tang.

ingredients_full.note: cubed, standing in for real melon

ingredients.note: cubed, standing in for real melon

steps_detailed: Simmer the squash in 1.5 cups water 15-18 minutes until it breaks down completely.
Whisk in the sorghum flour, stirring constantly, and simmer 10-12 minutes more until thick.

name: Batswana Pumpkin Leaves (Seswaa Lephala)
description: Pounded pumpkin leaves, cooked down until tender, are a genuine Batswana side dish - real pumpkin leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder approximation.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 3-4 minutes.
Add the spinach and a splash of water, and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Stir in the peanut butter and simmer 5 minutes more.

name: Batswana Vetkoek
description: Vetkoek, fried dough, shared with South Africa, a beloved Batswana snack often filled with mince.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and baking powder with warm water into a soft dough.
Let rest 15 minutes.
Shape into small balls and fry, turning, 4-5 minutes per batch, until deeply golden.

name: Batswana Chakalaka
description: Chakalaka, a spicy vegetable relish, is a beloved side shared with South Africa, common alongside pap and seswaa.
steps_detailed: Simmer the carrot, bell pepper, tomatoes, and curry powder together 12-15 minutes until the vegetables are tender but still have real bite.

name: Batswana Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Batswana home cooking outside the traditional seswaa preparation.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Batswana Grilled Boerewors
description: Boerewors, a coiled, spiced sausage, is shared with South Africa and a beloved Batswana braai staple.
steps_detailed: Grill the boerewors, coiled, over medium-high heat, turning once, 12-15 minutes, until cooked through and well charred.

name: Batswana Fried Sweet Potato
description: Simple fried sweet potato, a common Batswana snack.
steps_detailed: Fry the sweet potato wedges, turning, 6-8 minutes, until golden and tender inside.
Season with salt while still hot.

name: Batswana Coleslaw
description: A mayonnaise-dressed cabbage salad, a common Batswana side, real versions with a touch of mustard for depth.
steps_detailed: Whisk the mayonnaise and mustard together.
Toss with the cabbage and carrot until well coated.

name: Batswana Milk Tea
description: Sweetened milk tea is a beloved daily ritual across Botswana.
steps_detailed: Warm the tea and milk together 5 minutes.
Stir in the sugar before serving.

name: Batswana Tomato Onion Relish
description: A simple tomato-onion relish, a common Batswana condiment.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 12-15 minutes until thickened.
